messages:
maria: Hey team — ACME wants a short POC. They need Hosted API keys for devs + a temporary workspace with RBAC (3 dev seats) and an infra user who can later be granted Dedicated pool access. They also asked about Private/VPC options for later. Security requested short-lived tokens and IP allowlist. Can engineering outline the minimal steps and any cost/constraints?

alex: Quick clarifying q: for Hosted keys, do they want per-user keys or a workspace-level key scoped to roles?

maria: Prefer per-user dev keys if possible, but strictly least-privilege: devs only call generate/chat/embeddings. Infra user needs Dedicated provisioning rights.

sam: We have a flow that covers ephemeral invites + scoped API keys. I can drop the template. Also need the expected QPS so we can size Dedicated later.

sam: Link: https://internal.redwood/poc-templates/ephemeral-invites (use the "temp_invite" role and TTL fields).

tara: Security side: for Private/VPC we need customer subnet CIDR, peering window, and KMS CMK ARN for any managed keys. They prefer token rotation every 24h for POCs. Is that doable?

alex: Yes — Hosted supports IP allowlist + token TTL on API tokens. For Dedicated we can create a pool and grant the infra user a `dedicated.admin` scoped role. Proposed minimal steps: 1) create temp workspace with 7d expiry; 2) invite devs with `dev.poc` role (least privilege); 3) enable IP allowlist and token TTL; 4) provision Dedicated pool if requested and map infra user; 5) collect CIDR/KMS info if they want Private.

maria: Cost Qs: customer wants to know if Dedicated is billed pro rata for partial months, and if switching Hosted->Private requires model migration work.

sam: Dedicated reservations are pro rata from the start of the reservation. I'll pull exact billing language and a sample estimate. Model migration: generally yes — we snapshot model version and redeploy to Private; watch for quantization/compatibility differences. I'll confirm specifics for their chosen model.

tara: Security questionnaire item: "Do you support SAML group sync for RBAC?" Answer: yes, via SCIM with group->role mapping. Note that SCIM provisioning requires SAML/SCIM enabled on their IdP.

alex: Drafting a tiny runbook + example invite script now. Example commands (dev-friendly):
```
# create workspace
redwoodctl workspace create --name "acme-poc-temp" --expiry 7d
# invite devs
redwoodctl invite add --workspace acme-poc-temp --email dev1@acme.com --role dev.poc --expires 168h
# set token rotation
redwoodctl token rotate --workspace acme-poc-temp --ttl 24h
# enable IP allowlist
redwoodctl workspace update --workspace acme-poc-temp --ip-allowlist 203.0.113.0/24
```

maria: Nice. Can you also include a Dedicated pool sizing estimate for ~200 rps burst generation (short windows) so procurement has a number?

alex: Ballpark: 2x A100-style nodes should cover ~200rps for short-gen workloads; will vary by model/sequence length. I'll mark as ballpark and Sam will confirm price.

sam: I'll assemble pricing (pro rata calc + example) and add a short note about SLA tiers. Also prepping a trimmed security snapshot for their questionnaire with KMS/IP-allowlist/SAML answers.

deploy-bot: POC workspace acme-poc-temp created by alex at workspace id rwk_abc123 (expires in 7d).

maria: Great — tagging @tara for final signoff on the questionnaire answers. We'll send this to ACME and schedule a 30m kickoff tomorrow 10am PT.

tara: I'll review & add KMS/IP allowlist wording. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks everyone — once Sam posts the pricing I'll loop in procurement and legal for the minimal SOW/POC terms.
